title: Design the Right Chip: Why Prototyping Has to Be Easy
gist: A sponsored S2C piece argues that specification errors, not implementation bugs, are the unsolved part of chip verification (Wilson data shows incorrect or incomplete specs flat near 59%), so fast, portable FPGA prototyping that can be shown to customers early is the fix. It then markets S2C's Prodigy hardware and PlayerPro tools on four ease-of-use pillars.

insights.claim: Across Wilson Research Group studies, design error as a root cause of ASIC functional flaws fell from 75% to 60% between 2016 and 2024, and changes in specification fell from 59% to 43%.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Verification tooling is working on implementation errors, so incremental spend there has diminishing returns.

insights.claim: Incorrect or incomplete specification as a root cause of ASIC flaws went from 56% to 58% to 59% over three Wilson studies, essentially flat to slightly worse, so the industry has made no progress on building the right chip.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The unaddressed failure mode is where new verification and prototyping value accrues.
insights.quote: The industry has made no comparable progress on the first half.

insights.claim: Simulation, emulation, formal and constrained-random verification take the specification as given, so they cannot catch a misunderstood requirement that the testbench itself encodes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Specification-level risk needs different tools than conventional verification flows.
insights.quote: A misunderstood requirement cannot be caught by anything that encodes the same misunderstanding.

insights.claim: FPGA prototypes placed in front of customers, partners or standards bodies while the spec is still soft can expose specification errors such as wrong traffic-model buffer sizing, unmeetable latency budgets or unimplemented assumed-mandatory modes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Prototyping vendors can pitch customer-facing validation, not only software bring-up.
insights.locator: Shift left, further left than software

insights.claim: Software shift-left typically starts the software team six to nine months before first silicon, but specification is soft much earlier, at architecture definition, where the expensive decisions are made.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Value of prototyping rises the earlier it can be stood up.
insights.locator: Shift left, further left than software

insights.claim: Once the value lies in running systems early, repeatedly and in someone else's building, capacity becomes table stakes and ease of use (system environment, debugging, complex design, ecosystem) becomes the gating factor in a prototyping platform.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Competitive differentiation in prototyping is shifting from raw gate capacity to usability.
insights.locator: Shift left, further left than software

insights.claim: S2C offers 100+ Prototype Ready daughter cards and reference designs and 50+ Prototype Ready IP blocks, and Prodigy systems can be crated, shipped and recommissioned at customer sites or trade-show booths.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Portability is S2C's claimed edge over rack-bound emulators.

insights.claim: Prodigy's debug uses virtual JTAG instead of a physical cable, multi-FPGA-aware debug IP, and a PCIe AXI transactor (ProtoBridge), which S2C says can shrink debug loops from days to minutes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vendor claim; debug turnaround is a key metric to test in evaluations.

insights.claim: PlayerPro-CompileTime automates RTL-to-bitstream including partitioning, with speed bridges for PCIe and 10G to 400G Ethernet and memory models bridging DDR5, LPDDR5 and HBM3 controllers to board-mounted DDR4.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Automation of partitioning and speed bridging is where in-house flows break.
insights.quote: This is the difference between “the design fits” and “the design runs.”

insights.claim: The Prodigy Logic System S8-100, built on the AMD Versal Premium VP1902, carries roughly 100 million ASIC gates per core module, scaling to about 200 million with two modules and 400 million with four, with 2,212 XPIOs at up to 56Gbps.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Capacity specs set the ceiling for SoC sizes prototypable on a single S2C system.

insights.claim: In large multi-FPGA designs partitioning can hit a pin wall before logic capacity is exhausted, and TDM eases pin limits but can reduce effective bandwidth and add latency that affects the timing behavior being evaluated.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: I/O count, not gate count, can be the binding spec when comparing prototyping platforms.

insights.claim: S2C says it has pre-validated subsystems with Arm, Andes (AX46MPV, AX66 RISC-V), BOSC (16-core RISC-V), Sirius (Wi-Fi 6/Bluetooth RF) and XuanTie (C925), so many subsystems are exercised on Prodigy before customer RTL arrives.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: RISC-V ecosystem ties show where S2C is positioned in the China and RISC-V design flow.

insights.claim: S2C claims more than 20 years in ASIC/SoC verification, 300+ employees, 700+ customers, and service to 12 of the world's top 25 semiconductor companies since 2020.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: S2C estimates total cost of ownership at 30-50% below legacy EDA suppliers, enabling a prototype per need, including at customer facilities, rather than one shared box per site.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Unverified vendor claim of price pressure on incumbent EDA hardware-assisted verification.
